records.source: שׁ֤וּבִי שׁ֨וּבִי֙ הַשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית שׁ֥וּבִי שׁ֖וּבִי וְנֶחֱזֶה־בָּ֑ךְ מַֽה־תֶּחֱזוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וּלַמִּ֔ית כִּמְחֹלַ֖ת הַֽמַּחֲנָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Return, return, the Shulammite; return, return, and we will look at you. Why will you look at the Shulammite as at [the] dance of the two camps?
pieces: Come back, come back, Shulammite; \q come back, come back, so that we may look at you! \q Why do you want to look at the Shulammite \q as at the dance of Mahanaim?

L.1: Return, return, Shulammite; \q return, return, that we may look at you! \q Why will you look at the Shulammite \q as at the dance of Mahanaim?

R.1: Come back, come back, Shulammite! \q Come back, come back, so we can look at you! \q Why do you want to stare at the Shulammite \q as if she were dancing the dance of Mahanaim?

decisions.choice: This verse is 7:1 in the Hebrew text, 6:13 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 7 with this verse. Many Bibles number it 6:13, so their 7:1-13 is 7:2-14 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates.

decisions.choice: two voices: a group calls her, and someone answers
alternatives: the women of Jerusalem and the woman
decisions.reason: In the first half a group ("we") calls to the woman ("you" is feminine). The second half answers with a plural "you": it may be the woman herself, or the man, asking why they want to stare at her. The poem does not name either voice.

decisions.choice: the Shulammite: the woman from Shulem, or a name like Solomon's
decisions.reason: The word has the article: "the Shulammite". It may mean a woman from a town called Shulem or Shunem (compare Abishag the Shunammite, 1 Kings 1:3). It may also be a feminine form of the name Solomon, "the Solomon-woman", or come from the word for peace and wholeness. This is the only place she is named.

decisions.choice: the dance of Mahanaim: a famous dance, or a dance between two rows
alternatives: the dance of the two camps
decisions.reason: Mahanaim means "two camps" and is the name of a town east of the Jordan (Genesis 32:3; 2 Samuel 17:24). The words may name a dance known from there, or a dance between two rows of dancers or two companies. Either way, she is pictured as a dancer whom everyone watches; the praise that follows starts from her feet.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim
decisions.reason: The name is kept at every level, with its meaning given in a decision (m4), as for the other places in the Song.

records.heading: Come back, Shulammite

records.source: מַה־יָּפ֧וּ פְעָמַ֛יִךְ בַּנְּעָלִ֖ים בַּת־נָדִ֑יב חַמּוּקֵ֣י יְרֵכַ֔יִךְ כְּמ֣וֹ חֲלָאִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י אָמָּֽן׃
records.gloss: How beautiful are your feet in the sandals, daughter of a noble; [the] curves of your thighs [are] like ornaments, [the] work of [the] hands of a craftsman.
pieces: How beautiful your feet are in sandals, noble daughter! \q The curves of your thighs are like jewels, \q the work of a master craftsman.

L.2: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, daughter of a noble! \q The curves of your thighs [are] like jewels, \q the work of the hands of a craftsman.

R.2: Noble woman, your feet look beautiful in your sandals! \q The curves of your thighs are like jewels \q made by a skilled artist.

decisions.choice: This verse is 7:2 in the Hebrew text, 7:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: Because the Hebrew text counts 6:13 of those Bibles as 7:1, each verse of this chapter is numbered one higher here than in them: Hebrew 7:2-14 is 7:1-13.

decisions.choice: the man speaks (7:2-10)
decisions.reason: "Your" is feminine; the one who praises her is the man, as the words "I said" (7:9) and the rest of the song show.

decisions.choice: a third song in praise of her body (7:2-10)
decisions.reason: This time the man begins with her feet and goes up to her head (7:2-6), as one would look at a dancer (7:1). The comparisons speak of fine craft, of food and wine, and of the land's great places.

decisions.choice: daughter of a noble: noble woman
decisions.reason: "Daughter of" a quality means someone who has it. The word for noble is the same as in 6:12.

decisions.choice: curves of your thighs like jewels: shapely, as if made by an artist
decisions.reason: The rounded curve of her hips and thighs is like fine jewelry shaped by a master craftsman's hands. The image is kept at every level.

records.source: שָׁרְרֵךְ֙ אַגַּ֣ן הַסַּ֔הַר אַל־יֶחְסַ֖ר הַמָּ֑זֶג בִּטְנֵךְ֙ עֲרֵמַ֣ת חִטִּ֔ים סוּגָ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Your navel [is] a bowl of the roundness; let it not lack the mixed wine; your belly [is] a heap of wheat fenced with the lilies.
pieces: Your navel is a rounded bowl; \q may it never lack spiced wine. \q Your belly is a heap of wheat \q bordered with lilies.

L.3: Your navel [is] a rounded bowl; \q may it never lack mixed wine. \q Your belly [is] a heap of wheat \q fenced in with lilies.

R.3: Your navel is like a round bowl. \q May it always be full of wine. \q Your belly is like a heap of wheat \q with lilies all around it.

decisions.choice: your navel
decisions.reason: The word means the navel, or the cord at the navel (Ezekiel 16:4; Proverbs 3:8). Some think that here it refers to a more intimate part of her body; the word is kept as it is, and the image is no more explicit than the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: a rounded bowl that never lacks mixed wine
decisions.reason: Her navel is round like a fine bowl, and the bowl is full of mixed wine, wine blended with water or spices for a feast. Wine is a picture of the delight of love (1:2; 7:10).

decisions.choice: a heap of wheat fenced with lilies: rounded, golden and rich
decisions.reason: A heap of threshed wheat is smooth, rounded and the color of warm skin, and it is the wealth of harvest. The lilies around it are a border of flowers. The image is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: spiced wine
decisions.reason: "Mixed wine" was usually wine blended with spices (Proverbs 9:2; Isaiah 5:22); Balanced says "spiced".

records.source: שְׁנֵ֥י שָׁדַ֛יִךְ כִּשְׁנֵ֥י עֳפָרִ֖ים תָּאֳמֵ֥י צְבִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Your two breasts [are] like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
pieces: Your breasts are like two fawns, \q the twins of a gazelle.

L.4: Your two breasts [are] like two fawns, \q twins of a gazelle.

R.4: Your breasts are like two young deer, \q twin fawns of a gazelle.

decisions.choice: as 4:5
decisions.reason: The words repeat 4:5, without the lilies; the meaning of the picture is given there.

decisions.choice: as 4:5
decisions.reason: Worded as in 4:5 at each level. The verse has no main division; the line break follows its only dividing accent, after "fawns".

records.source: צַוָּארֵ֖ךְ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַשֵּׁ֑ן עֵינַ֜יִךְ בְּרֵכ֣וֹת בְּחֶשְׁבּ֗וֹן עַל־שַׁ֨עַר֙ בַּת־רַבִּ֔ים אַפֵּךְ֙ כְּמִגְדַּ֣ל הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן צוֹפֶ֖ה פְּנֵ֥י דַמָּֽשֶׂק׃
records.gloss: Your neck [is] like a tower of the ivory; your eyes [are] pools in Heshbon by [the] gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose [is] like [the] tower of the Lebanon, looking toward Damascus.
pieces: Your neck is like an ivory tower; \q your eyes are the pools of Heshbon beside the gate of Bath-rabbim; \q your nose is like Lebanon's tower \q that looks out toward Damascus.

L.5: Your neck [is] like the tower of ivory; \q your eyes [are] pools in Heshbon at the gate of Bath-rabbim; \q your nose [is] as the tower of the Lebanon \q looking toward Damascus.

R.5: Your neck is like a tower of ivory. \q Your eyes are as clear as the pools in Heshbon, beside the gate of Bath-rabbim. \q Your nose is like Lebanon's tower \q that looks out toward Damascus.

decisions.choice: your neck like an ivory tower: tall, smooth and pale
decisions.reason: As in 4:4, her neck is a tower; here it is ivory, smooth and costly (5:14).

decisions.choice: your eyes like the pools of Heshbon: clear, deep and still
decisions.reason: Heshbon was a city east of the Jordan, once the capital of King Sihon (Numbers 21:26), on the high plain where water had to be stored in pools. Bath-rabbim ("daughter of many") seems to be the name of one of its gates; it is not known from elsewhere. Her eyes are like water that is clear and shining.

decisions.choice: your nose like the tower of Lebanon facing Damascus: noble and strong
decisions.reason: A tower on the heights of Lebanon would look out over the land toward Damascus, the capital of Aram to the northeast. The picture praises the dignity of her face, its straight, fine line; it is not about size.

decisions.choice: as clear as the pools
decisions.reason: Readable adds "clear" to give the point of the comparison (m2).

records.source: רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ כַּכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְדַלַּ֥ת רֹאשֵׁ֖ךְ כָּאַרְגָּמָ֑ן מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר בָּרְהָטִֽים׃
records.gloss: Your head upon you [is] like Carmel, and [the] hair of your head like purple; a king is held captive in the tresses.
pieces: Your head crowns you like Carmel, \q and your flowing hair is like purple; \q a king is held captive by its locks.

L.6: Your head upon you [is] like Carmel, \q and the hair of your head [is] like purple; \q a king is held captive in the tresses.

R.6: Your head is as majestic as Mount Carmel. \q Your hair shines like purple cloth. \q Its locks have captured a king.

decisions.choice: your head like Carmel: crowning and splendid
decisions.reason: Mount Carmel is the wooded ridge that rises over the sea in the northwest of the land, known for its beauty (Isaiah 35:2). Her head rises above her body as Carmel rises over the coast. The name also sounds like the word for a fruitful garden.

decisions.choice: your hair like purple: dark with a rich sheen
decisions.reason: Purple dye was deep red-violet and was worn by kings (3:10). Her dark hair gleams with the richness of royal cloth.

decisions.choice: a king held captive in the tresses: he is caught by her
decisions.reason: The word for tresses is used of water troughs (Genesis 30:38), perhaps for the flowing locks of her hair. The king, the man who speaks, is held captive by them.

decisions.choice: as majestic as Mount Carmel
alternatives: your head upon you is like Carmel
decisions.reason: Readable says what the comparison means and that Carmel is a mountain (m1).

records.gloss: How beautiful you are and how pleasant you are, love, with the delights!
pieces: How beautiful and how pleasing you are, \q love, with all your delights!

L.7: How beautiful you are, and how pleasant, \q love, with [its] delights!

R.7: You are so beautiful and so pleasing! \q Love, you fill me with delight!

decisions.choice: love, with its delights: he speaks to her as "love"
alternatives: my loved one, daughter of delights
decisions.reason: He calls her "love" itself, a love full of delights. Some read the word with other vowels as "loved one", and read the next words as "daughter of delights" (with a change of division found in some ancient versions).

decisions.choice: all your delights
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "your", since he is speaking to her.

records.source: זֹ֤את קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙ דָּֽמְתָ֣ה לְתָמָ֔ר וְשָׁדַ֖יִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: This your stature is like to a palm tree, and your breasts to clusters.
pieces: You are as tall as a palm tree, \q and your breasts are like its clusters of fruit.

L.8: This stature of yours is like a palm tree, \q and your breasts [are] like clusters.

R.8: You are tall and slender like a palm tree. \q Your breasts are like clusters of dates.

decisions.choice: your stature like a palm tree: tall and graceful
decisions.reason: The date palm grows tall, straight and slender. Tamar, the word for palm, was also a woman's name (Genesis 38:6; 2 Samuel 13:1).

decisions.choice: your breasts like clusters: the palm's fruit
decisions.reason: The clusters of a date palm hang high and full of sweet fruit. The image is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: clusters of dates
decisions.reason: Readable says what the palm's clusters are (m2).

records.source: אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶעֱלֶ֣ה בְתָמָ֔ר אֹֽחֲזָ֖ה בְּסַנְסִנָּ֑יו וְיִֽהְיוּ־נָ֤א שָׁדַ֨יִךְ֙ כְּאֶשְׁכְּל֣וֹת הַגֶּ֔פֶן וְרֵ֥יחַ אַפֵּ֖ךְ כַּתַּפּוּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: I said: I will climb on [the] palm tree, I will take hold of its fruit stalks; and may be, please, your breasts like clusters of the vine, and [the] scent of your breath like the apples,
pieces: I said: I will climb the palm tree \q and take hold of its branches of fruit. \q Oh, may your breasts be like clusters of grapes, \q and the scent of your breath like apples,

L.9: I said: I will go up into the palm tree; \q I will grasp its fruit stalks. \q Oh, may your breasts be like clusters of the vine, \q and the scent of your breath like apples,

R.9: I said to myself, I will climb that palm tree \q and take hold of its fruit. \q May your breasts be like bunches of grapes. \q May your breath smell sweet like apples.

decisions.choice: I said: I decided
decisions.reason: "I said" here means "I said to myself", "I decided" (Psalm 32:5). It reports his resolve, not words spoken to someone else.

decisions.choice: I will climb the palm and take hold of its fruit: his desire to embrace her
decisions.reason: Having pictured her as a palm tree (7:8), he says he will climb it and take hold of its fruit: he longs to hold her. The image is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: clusters of the vine ... breath like apples: sweetness and fragrance
decisions.reason: The clusters are now grapes, full and sweet. "Breath" is literally "nose"; the scent of her breath is as sweet as apples (2:3, 5).

decisions.choice: no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Because "I said" reports his own resolve (m1), his words take no quotation marks; a colon introduces them at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: breath
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "the scent of your nose"; English says "breath".

records.source: וְחִכֵּ֕ךְ כְּיֵ֥ין הַטּ֛וֹב הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: and your palate like wine of the best, going to my beloved smoothly, gliding [over the] lips of sleepers.
pieces: and your mouth like the finest wine, \q flowing smoothly to my beloved, \q gliding over the lips of those who sleep.

L.10: and your mouth like the best wine \q that goes down smoothly to my beloved, \q gliding over the lips of sleepers.

R.10: May your mouth taste like the best wine. \q Let it flow smoothly to my love, \q gliding over the lips of those who sleep.

decisions.choice: the woman takes up his words
decisions.reason: "To my beloved" is the woman's word for the man. So in the middle of the verse she breaks in: he says that her mouth is like the best wine, and she answers that this wine flows to her beloved. Where exactly her words begin is not certain.

decisions.choice: your mouth like the best wine: her kisses
decisions.reason: The mouth (the palate, as 5:16) is like fine wine: her kisses are sweet and heady (1:2; 4:10).

decisions.choice: smoothly
decisions.reason: The same word as "rightly" in 1:4; here it means wine that goes down easily (Proverbs 23:31).

decisions.choice: the lips of sleepers
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "the lips of sleepers": the wine glides over the lips of the lovers as they drowse. The Greek and Syriac translations read "my lips and teeth", from a different reading of the same letters.

decisions.choice: May your mouth taste like the best wine
decisions.reason: Readable continues the wish of 7:9 as a new sentence.

records.gloss: I [am] my beloved's, and for me [is] his desire.
pieces: I am my beloved's, \q and his desire is for me.

L.11: I [am] my beloved's, \q and for me [is] his desire.

R.11: I belong to my love, \q and he longs for me.

decisions.choice: the woman speaks (7:11-14)
decisions.reason: She says "my beloved" and speaks to him in 7:12.

decisions.choice: his desire is for me: the word of Genesis 3:16
decisions.reason: The word for desire (teshuqah) is rare; in Genesis 3:16 it is the woman's desire for her husband, who "will rule over" her. Here the desire is his, for her, and there is no ruling: love is mutual.

decisions.choice: the third saying of belonging
decisions.reason: After 2:16 and 6:3, she says a third time that she belongs to him; this time the second line is his longing for her.

decisions.choice: as 6:3
decisions.reason: "I am my beloved's" is worded as in 6:3 at each level.

records.source: לְכָ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ נֵצֵ֣א הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה נָלִ֖ינָה בַּכְּפָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Come, my beloved, let us go out [to] the field; let us spend the night in the villages.
pieces: Come, my beloved, let us go out into the country \q and spend the night in the villages.

L.12: Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field; \q let us spend the night in the villages.

R.12: Come, my love, let us go out into the country \q and spend the night in the villages.

decisions.choice: she speaks to him
decisions.reason: "Come" is masculine; she invites her beloved.

decisions.choice: the villages: or the henna bushes
decisions.reason: The word can be the plural of "village" or of "henna" (1:14; 4:13). Out in the fields, the henna bushes are as likely a place to spend the night as the villages.

records.heading: She invites him to the fields

records.source: נַשְׁכִּ֨ימָה֙ לַכְּרָמִ֔ים נִרְאֶ֞ה אִם פָּֽרְחָ֤ה הַגֶּ֨פֶן֙ פִּתַּ֣ח הַסְּמָדַ֔ר הֵנֵ֖צוּ הָרִמּוֹנִ֑ים שָׁ֛ם אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Let us go early to the vineyards; let us see whether has budded the vine, has opened the blossom, have bloomed the pomegranates; there I will give my lovemaking to you.
pieces: Let us go early to the vineyards \q to see if the vines have budded and their blossoms opened, \q and if the pomegranates are in flower. \q There I will give my love to you.

L.13: Let us rise early [and go] to the vineyards; \q let us see whether the vine has budded, whether its blossom has opened, \q whether the pomegranates have bloomed. \q There I will give my lovemaking to you.

R.13: Let us get up early and go to the vineyards. \q Let us see if the grapevines have buds and their blossoms have opened, \q and if the pomegranate trees are blooming. \q There I will give you my love.

decisions.choice: the spring of 2:11-13 and 6:11
decisions.reason: She asks him to go and see what he called her to see in 2:13, and what one of them went to see in 6:11: the land in flower, ready for love.

decisions.choice: my lovemaking
decisions.reason: As 1:2. She promises to give him her love there.

decisions.choice: to you
decisions.reason: The form of "to you" is the one used at a pause in the verse; she is speaking to him.

decisions.choice: my love

records.source: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים נָֽתְנוּ־רֵ֗יחַ וְעַל־פְּתָחֵ֨ינוּ֙ כָּל־מְגָדִ֔ים חֲדָשִׁ֖ים גַּם־יְשָׁנִ֑ים דּוֹדִ֖י צָפַ֥נְתִּי לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: The mandrakes give fragrance, and over our doors [are] all choice fruits, new as well as old; my beloved, I have stored [them] up for you.
pieces: The mandrakes give off their scent, and at our doors are all kinds of choice fruits, \q new as well as old, \q which I have saved for you, my beloved.

L.14: The mandrakes give off fragrance, and over our doors [are] all choice fruits, \q new as well as old; \q my beloved, I have stored [them] up for you.

R.14: The mandrakes smell sweet. At our door are all kinds of the best fruits, \q new ones and old ones. \q My love, I have saved them for you.

decisions.choice: mandrakes: a plant believed to stir love
decisions.reason: The mandrake has a strong-smelling yellow fruit and a forked root. People believed it aroused love and helped a woman to conceive (Genesis 30:14-16). Its Hebrew name sounds like the word for lovemaking (7:13).

decisions.choice: choice fruits new and old over our doors: every delight kept for him
decisions.reason: Fruit was stored on shelves above the doorway, or hung at the door. She has saved up every kind of delight, fresh and long kept, for him (4:13, 16).

decisions.choice: for you
decisions.reason: As in 7:13, the form is the one used at a pause; she is speaking to him.
